items.followUp: Explain how biology is related to biochemistry and biogeography.

rubric.why: Award for explaining one valid link between biology and another science.
rubric.description: Biophysics applies the principles of physics to biological processes.
rubric.how: Name biophysics and state its connection with physics.

rubric.why: Award for explaining a second valid link.
rubric.description: Biochemistry applies the principles of chemistry to living organisms and their processes.
rubric.how: Name biochemistry and state its connection with chemistry.

rubric.why: Award for explaining a third valid link.
rubric.description: Biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
rubric.how: Name biogeography and describe what it studies.

rubric.why: Award for explaining any other valid link between biology and a science.
rubric.description: Bioeconomics relates biology to economics; biomathematics or biostatistics applies mathematical methods to biological data.
rubric.how: Name another biology-related field and state its connection.

modelAnswer: Biophysics applies the principles of physics to biological processes.
Biochemistry applies the principles of chemistry to living organisms and their processes.
Biogeography studies the geographical distribution of organisms.
Bioeconomics relates biological resources and processes to economics.

items.followUp: Give three differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.

rubric.why: Award for a correct distinction in nuclear organization.
rubric.description: Prokaryotic cells lack a membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotic cells have one.
rubric.how: Contrast the presence of a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Award for a correct distinction in genetic material.
rubric.description: Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular and not enclosed in a nucleus; eukaryotic DNA is linear and associated with proteins.
rubric.how: Contrast the form or organization of DNA.

rubric.why: Award for a correct distinction in cell organization.
rubric.description: Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells contain them.
rubric.how: Contrast the presence of membrane-bound organelles.

rubric.why: Award for a correct size comparison.
rubric.description: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller than eukaryotic cells.
rubric.how: State that prokaryotic cells are smaller and eukaryotic cells are larger.

rubric.why: Award for a correct distinction in cell division.
rubric.description: Prokaryotic cells divide by binary fission; eukaryotic cells divide by mitosis or meiosis.
rubric.how: Name the usual division method in each cell type.

modelAnswer: Prokaryotic cells have no membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotic cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Prokaryotic DNA is generally circular and not enclosed in a nucleus; eukaryotic DNA is linear and associated with proteins.
Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles; eukaryotic cells have membrane-bound organelles.
Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller than eukaryotic cells.
Prokaryotic cells divide by binary fission; eukaryotic cells divide by mitosis or meiosis.

items.followUp: Explain how temperature can affect enzyme activity.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the specific fit between enzyme and substrate.
rubric.description: An enzyme has an active site with a shape complementary to its specific substrate, like a lock and its key.
rubric.how: Describe the shape-specific fit of substrate and active site.

rubric.why: Award for describing the first stage of the mechanism.
rubric.description: The substrate fits into the active site and forms an enzyme-substrate complex.
rubric.how: State that binding forms an enzyme-substrate complex.

rubric.why: Award for explaining what happens to the substrate.
rubric.description: The enzyme catalyses the reaction, converting the substrate into product or products.
rubric.how: State that the bound substrate is changed into products.

rubric.why: Award for noting that the enzyme remains available after the reaction.
rubric.description: The products leave the active site; the enzyme is unchanged and can be used again.
rubric.how: State that the enzyme is not used up and can catalyse another reaction.

modelAnswer: An enzyme has an active site with a shape complementary to its specific substrate, like a lock and its key.
The substrate fits into the active site and forms an enzyme-substrate complex.
The enzyme catalyses the reaction, changing the substrate into product or products.
The products leave the active site; the enzyme remains unchanged and can be used again.

items.followUp: Write the word equation for photosynthesis and state one difference between photosynthesis and respiration.

rubric.why: Award for a correct definition of photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy and chlorophyll to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
rubric.how: Define the process and identify its essential inputs and energy source.

rubric.why: Award for a correct contrast in main cellular site.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts; respiration occurs mainly in mitochondria.
rubric.how: Contrast the main organelles where the processes occur.

rubric.why: Award for correctly contrasting the materials used and formed.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water to make glucose and oxygen; respiration uses glucose and oxygen and forms carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.how: Contrast the reactants and products of the two processes.

rubric.why: Award for a correct contrast in energy change.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis stores energy in glucose; respiration releases energy from food.
rubric.how: Contrast energy storage with energy release.

rubric.why: Award for a further valid contrast in conditions or occurrence.
rubric.description: Photosynthesis requires light and occurs in photosynthetic cells; respiration occurs continuously in living cells.
rubric.how: State a valid contrast in light requirement or occurrence.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy and chlorophyll to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, releasing oxygen.
Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, whereas respiration occurs mainly in mitochondria.
Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water and forms glucose and oxygen; respiration uses glucose and oxygen and forms carbon dioxide and water.
Photosynthesis stores energy in glucose, whereas respiration releases energy from food.
Photosynthesis requires light, whereas respiration occurs continuously in living cells.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the subject of parasitology.
rubric.description: Parasitology is the branch of biology that studies parasites.
rubric.how: State that the field studies parasites.

rubric.why: Award for including the parasite-host relationship.
rubric.description: It also studies the relationships between parasites and their hosts.
rubric.how: Mention the interaction of parasites with their hosts.

modelAnswer: Parasitology is the branch of biology that studies parasites and their relationships with their hosts.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a tissue and an organ.

rubric.why: Award for correctly defining a population.
rubric.description: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
rubric.how: State the species, area and time features of a population.

rubric.why: Award for correctly distinguishing a community from a population.
rubric.description: A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.
rubric.how: State that a community includes different populations living together.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.
A community consists of populations of different species living and interacting in the same area.

items.followUp: Write the steps of the biological method in their usual order.

rubric.why: Award for naming the initial steps of the biological method.
rubric.description: The method begins with recognition of a biological problem, followed by observation and formulation of a hypothesis.
rubric.how: Name the problem, observation and hypothesis stages.

rubric.why: Award for naming the remaining main steps.
rubric.description: The remaining steps are deductions, experimentation, summarization of results and reporting.
rubric.how: Name the stages after hypothesis in their usual sequence.

modelAnswer: Recognition of a biological problem.
Observation.
Hypothesis.
Deductions.
Experimentation.
Summarization of results.
Reporting.

items.followUp: Write two observations that supported the idea that mosquitoes spread malaria.

rubric.why: Award for one relevant observation attributed to A.F.A. King.
rubric.description: People sleeping under mosquito nets were less likely to contract malaria.
rubric.how: State the observation linking protection from mosquito bites with reduced malaria.

rubric.why: Award for a second relevant observation attributed to A.F.A. King.
rubric.description: People sleeping outdoors or without mosquito nets were more likely to contract malaria.
rubric.how: State the contrasting observation about exposure to mosquitoes and malaria.

modelAnswer: People sleeping under mosquito nets were less likely to contract malaria.
People sleeping outdoors or in rooms without mosquito nets were more likely to contract malaria.
